text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Valentin Mollov, the director of Bulgaria's Mollov bank which was put under special supervision by the central bank on September 23, was stopped from boarding a plane to Vienna, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Citizens' deposits in insolvent banks will be fully repaid by the state no sooner than 30 days after the court declares the banks insolvent under amendments to the Deposit Guarantee Law approved by the parliament. Firms will be able to draw their lev deposits from insolvent banks 60 days after the court's ruling.
-- Deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev was appointed to head the Bank Consolidation Company, which manages state equity in commercial banks.

-- Big sums from the partly state-owned MIC insurance company were illegally siphoned abroad, the prosecutor's office in Plovdiv said. The former chief of the firm Hristo Draganov and Agrobusinessbank's former director Hristo Aleksandrov were arrested on charges of misappropriation last week.

-- The European Bank for Investment and Development, Raffeisenbank and the Italian Agricola bank said they were interested in buying a stake in Bulgaria's state-owned Expressbank, Expressbank's head Ivan Konstantinov said.
-- Bulgarian-Russian gas company Topenergy plans to invest $570 million in building a gas pipeline from Russia to Turkey, a company official said.
-- Bulgaria's Socialist party plans to propose amendments to the Bank and Credit Law to make public the country's credit millionaires, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Bulgaria's Confederation of the Independent Trade Unions will stage a 24-hour general strike on November 20 to protest against the social policy of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov's Socialist government, union leaders said.

-- The head of Bulgaria's state-owned Bulbank, Chavdar Kanchev, should have considered the state's interests rather than his own views as a banker, said socialist parliamentary group chairman Krasimir Premyanov. Last week Bulgaria lost a $25 million credit guarantee for the import of 120,000 tonnes of wheat after Bulbank refused to confirm the credit line on the grounds the conditions were unfavourable.

-- All politicians, former and current ministers and public personalities who made statements to the media about the assassination of former prime minister Andrei Lukanov will be questioned, a National Investigation Service source said.
